code_label: Future applicability to FX reserves management
text_span: it is proven that in principle it will be possible to apply such computers in FX reserves management in the future.
rationale: States the paper’s main conclusion about future feasibility in the target domain.

code_label: Educational introduction for regulators
text_span: the article serves as an introduction to quantum computing for the staff of central banks and financial market supervisory authorities.
rationale: Defines a secondary purpose of the paper beyond the technical demonstrations.

code_label: Quantum speed-up motivates finance applications
text_span: quantum algorithms offer significant speed-up (in other words, have lower complexity) in comparison with their classical counterparts.
rationale: Frames the general motivation for exploring quantum computing in finance.

code_label: Finance use cases identified
text_span: portfolio optimization [10], risk management [11] and [12], interest rate derivatives pricing [13], and machine learning [14].
rationale: Lists the finance tasks the author says quantum algorithms can support.

code_label: Paper focus on reserves management tasks
text_span: we will focus on the application of quantum computers in foreign exchange reserves management.
rationale: Specifies the paper’s application focus.

code_label: Algorithms selected for demonstration
text_span: risk measurement using the quantum Monte Carlo method and Markowitz-like portfolio optimization using a quantum linear equations solver (the HHL algorithm) and a quantum quadratic unconstrained binary optimization method (the quantum approximate optimization algorithm – QAOA).
rationale: Identifies the three algorithmic approaches used in the demonstrations.

code_label: Toy-model constraint from hardware maturity
text_span: the current early stage of quantum hardware development restricted us to toy models only
rationale: States a key practical limitation affecting the demonstrations.

code_label: Mixed empirical success across algorithms
text_span: we successfully carried out portfolio optimization with the QAOA employing five binary variables for all the cases tested.
rationale: Reports a successful result for one of the main demonstrations.

code_label: Risk and HHL failures on hardware
text_span: the application of the quantum Monte Carlo method to risk measurement generated only partially correct results, and the use of the HHL algorithm in portfolio optimization failed completely.
rationale: Summarizes the negative hardware results for two methods.

code_label: Simulator validation of implementations
text_span: running the algorithms discussed above on a quantum computer simulator ... proved that our implementations are correct
rationale: Indicates that simulator runs validated the code despite hardware issues.

code_label: Qubit superposition as basis of computation
text_span: a qubit can be in both states at once, written mathematically as |q⟩= α|0⟩+ β|1⟩,
locator: 2.1.1 Quantum Bits, Superposition, Entanglement, and Measurement
rationale: Introduces the foundational representation used throughout the paper.

code_label: Measurement is probabilistic collapse
text_span: the result of measurement is a probabilistic event
locator: 2.1.1 Quantum Bits, Superposition, Entanglement, and Measurement
rationale: Explains the measurement principle underlying all quantum outputs in the paper.

code_label: Entanglement as non-separable state
text_span: Such inseparable states are called entangled states.
locator: 2.1.1 Quantum Bits, Superposition, Entanglement, and Measurement
rationale: Defines a core quantum property used in later algorithms.

code_label: Quantum gates as unitary transformations
text_span: The matrix U in expression (12) is the mathematical representation of a quantum gate.
rationale: Establishes the operational model for the gate-based approach.

code_label: Bell-state circuit as example
text_span: the circuit is composed of a Hadamard gate located on the first qubit, followed by a CNOT gate.
rationale: Provides the paper’s basic circuit example for entanglement preparation.

code_label: Swap test used for inner products
text_span: A swap test is an algorithm allowing us to calculate the absolute value of the inner product of two quantum states
rationale: Introduces a post-processing tool used later in optimization contexts.

code_label: Swap test limitation on sign and complex parts
text_span: The main disadvantage of the swap test is its inability to determine the sign of the inner product
rationale: States an explicit methodological caveat.

code_label: QFT encodes binary strings into phases
text_span: the QFT encodes the input binary string and its sub-strings into quantum phases of the output qubits.
rationale: Describes the role of QFT in later algorithms, especially HHL.

code_label: Quantum risk method gives quadratic speed-up
text_span: An important benefit of this algorithm is that it provides quadratic speed-up in comparison with classical calculation techniques based on Monte Carlo simulation.
locator: 2.2.1 Calculating Risk Measures on a Quantum Computer
rationale: States the claimed computational advantage of the risk method.

code_label: Risk metrics encoded through measurement
text_span: the probability of measuring |1⟩ in the last qubit of | ˜ψ⟩ is the sum of the probabilities of all outcomes having shape |i⟩|1⟩
locator: 2.2.1 Calculating Risk Measures on a Quantum Computer
rationale: Explains the measurement-based mechanism for estimating expectations.

code_label: VaR computed by interval bisection
text_span: we combine quantum and classical (i.e., interval bisection) calculations.
locator: 2.2.1 Calculating Risk Measures on a Quantum Computer
rationale: Identifies the hybrid procedure used for VaR.

code_label: CVaR formula depends on VaR and conditional probability
text_span: CVaRα(X) = P1 VaRα(X) P[X ≤ VaRα(X)]
locator: 2.2.1 Calculating Risk Measures on a Quantum Computer
rationale: Captures the paper’s stated CVaR computation rule.

code_label: Controlled rotations require angle transformation
text_span: the rotational angles have to be adapted to this substituting configuration.
locator: 2.2.1 Calculating Risk Measures on a Quantum Computer
rationale: Notes a technical design choice in state preparation.

code_label: HHL solves linear systems via phase estimation
text_span: To solve A|x⟩= |b⟩ on a quantum computer, we need to prepare solution (41) as a quantum state.
locator: 2.2.2 Quantum Solver of Systems of Linear Equations
rationale: States the core objective of the HHL procedure.

code_label: HHL speed-up depends on sparsity and conditioning
text_span: The complexity of the algorithm is O[log(N)sκ/ϵ], where s is the sparsity of matrix A
locator: 2.2.2 Quantum Solver of Systems of Linear Equations
rationale: Identifies structural conditions that limit HHL performance.

code_label: Portfolio optimization translated to linear system
text_span: the optimization can be translated to the solution of a linear system
locator: 2.2.2 Quantum Solver of Systems of Linear Equations
rationale: Explains the mathematical reformulation used for HHL-based optimization.

code_label: HHL output used through inner products rather than full readout
text_span: To exploit the high performance of the HHL algorithm, we have to use the portfolio optimization results ... in other ways
locator: 2.2.2 Quantum Solver of Systems of Linear Equations
rationale: Describes the paper’s strategy to avoid full state tomography.

code_label: QUBO mapped to Ising Hamiltonian
text_span: QUBO is also useful in portfolio optimization.
rationale: Introduces the binary optimization framework used in the final demonstration.

code_label: No proof of QUBO superiority
text_span: there is no proof that quantum QUBO solvers are superior to classical solvers.
rationale: States an explicit caveat about the algorithmic claim.

code_label: QAOA is a hybrid algorithm
text_span: We clearly see that the QAOA is a hybrid algorithm.
rationale: Characterizes the algorithmic structure of QAOA.

code_label: Binary portfolio objective combines return, risk, and budget
text_span: Our aim is simultaneously to maximize the portfolio return ... to minimize risk ... and to invest the whole budget
rationale: Summarizes the optimization target used in the QAOA application.

code_label: Hardware noise and decoherence as major obstacle
text_span: some further development is necessary.
locator: 3.1 Notes on the Current State of Development of Quantum Hardware
rationale: Captures the paper’s central hardware caveat in the practical section.

code_label: Limited qubit connectivity increases circuit complexity
text_span: If we want to establish a line of communication between two qubits that are not directly connected, we have to use intermediate qubits and swap gates.
locator: 3.1 Notes on the Current State of Development of Quantum Hardware
rationale: Describes a hardware constraint affecting circuit implementation.

code_label: qRAM absent and needed for practical speed-up
text_span: there is currently no functional quantum equivalent to an operational memory (quantum RAM or qRAM).
locator: 3.1 Notes on the Current State of Development of Quantum Hardware
rationale: States a major missing infrastructure component.

code_label: Quantum volume as benchmark but imperfect
text_span: quantum volume is a somewhat artificial benchmark
locator: 3.1 Notes on the Current State of Development of Quantum Hardware
rationale: Notes a caveat about the benchmark used to compare processors.

code_label: Risk algorithm validated on simulator
text_span: the results are in accordance with the classical calculation presented in Table 2.
locator: 3.2 Measuring Risk in a Fixed-Income Portfolio
rationale: Reports simulator agreement with classical risk calculations.

code_label: Hardware risk results mixed and often wrong
text_span: the evaluation of the standard deviation and the 95% VaR is totally incorrect.
locator: 3.2 Measuring Risk in a Fixed-Income Portfolio
rationale: Summarizes the main negative hardware outcome for risk estimation.

code_label: Expected value more robust than tail metrics
text_span: the expected value was calculated almost correctly for both the three- and four-qubit states
locator: 3.2 Measuring Risk in a Fixed-Income Portfolio
rationale: Highlights the one risk metric that performed relatively well on hardware.

code_label: Lower percentiles limited by angle resolution
text_span: the rotational angles get smaller and the diﬀerence in the angles between consecutive iterations of the algorithm is below the lowest distinguishable level.
locator: 3.2 Measuring Risk in a Fixed-Income Portfolio
rationale: Explains a technical reason for VaR failure.

code_label: Qubit connectivity affects error mitigation
text_span: Qubit connectivity plays an important role in error mitigation.
locator: 3.2 Measuring Risk in a Fixed-Income Portfolio
rationale: Identifies a hardware factor influencing results across experiments.

code_label: HHL failed on target portfolio optimization
text_span: we obtained totally wrong results – wﬁx. inc = 10.29% and wequity = 18.41%.
locator: 3.3 Finding the Optimal Balance Between Bonds and Equities
rationale: Reports the failed HHL output for the main portfolio task.

code_label: Positive-eigenvalue restriction in implementation
text_span: the current Qiskit implementation of the HHL algorithm is only able to work with matrices where all the eigenvalues are positive.
locator: 3.3 Finding the Optimal Balance Between Bonds and Equities
rationale: States a software limitation discovered during debugging.

code_label: Deep circuits make HHL unusable on hardware
text_span: the circuit width was 159 gates.
locator: 3.3 Finding the Optimal Balance Between Bonds and Equities
rationale: Shows the scale of the circuit contributing to hardware failure.

code_label: QAOA succeeded on all available processors
text_span: We carried out the calculation on all the available five-qubit real quantum processors with success.
rationale: Reports successful execution of the QAOA demonstration.

code_label: QAOA required many iterations
text_span: the number of iterations needed to find the solution was higher than the number of possible solutions of the task
rationale: Notes an efficiency observation from the QAOA runs.

code_label: QAOA performance linked to quantum volume
text_span: The number of iterations depends on the quantum volume of the processor
rationale: Connects algorithm performance to hardware benchmark.

code_label: Application-oriented benchmarking preferred
text_span: we should assess the quality of the current quantum processors based on a particular application and not only on a single number like the quantum volume
rationale: States a methodological recommendation about benchmarking.

code_label: Simulator results support correctness of all algorithms
text_span: all the results obtained were in accordance with those obtained using classical methods.
rationale: Summarizes simulator validation across the paper’s methods.

code_label: QAOA likely first practical finance use
text_span: it seems that binary optimization will be among the first real-world problems that quantum computers are used for.
rationale: Projects a likely near-term application area.

code_label: Need for better hardware and qRAM
text_span: decoherence times and the number of qubits have to be increased, gate fidelity has to be improved, and, above all, a functional qRAM has to be built.
rationale: Lists the main future technical requirements.
